hints: Notice the oil drop has both mass and charge and sits in the uniform field between the top plate and bottom plate.
Recall weight $W = mg$ always acts downwards on a mass, while a charge $Q$ in field $E$ feels $F = EQ$.
Use the word stationary to connect the physics: for zero resultant force the upward electric force must balance the downward weight.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: a charged oil drop of mass $m$ and charge $Q$ placed between charged parallel plates that produce a vertical electric field $E$.
State the gravitational effect: Earth pulls the mass downwards with weight $W = mg$, which acts even when the plates are charged.
State the electric effect: the charge in the field feels an electric force $F = EQ$, directed to oppose the weight so the plates can support the drop.
Apply equilibrium for a stationary object: resultant force is zero, so the upward electric force must equal the downward weight in magnitude.
Therefore both forces act at the same time to cancel out. This is option A.

options.A: The drop has weight $W = mg$ downwards and electric force $F = EQ$ upwards that balance to hold it stationary.
options.B: An electric force alone would give a resultant force and accelerate the drop, so weight must also act downwards.
options.C: Weight alone would make the drop fall, so an upward electric force from the charged plates must also act.
options.D: The oil drop has mass and charge in an electric field, so both gravitational and electric forces cannot be zero.
